<h1 align="center">CASTAWAY</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>How many hours(0-15)? 10</b><br>
  A ten-hour lo-fi island video in which she idles, and every so often, something happens.<br>
  Then it asks whether you would like to wait another bar. Answer N and it asks how many hours again.
</p>

<p align="center">
  <kbd>f1</kbd>&nbsp;<a href="tools/serve.py">serve</a> &nbsp;
  <kbd>f2</kbd>&nbsp;<a href="activities.toml">list</a> &nbsp;
  <kbd>f3</kbd>&nbsp;<a href="tools/schedule.py">schedule</a> &nbsp;
  <kbd>f4</kbd>&nbsp;<a href="tools/make_audio.py">sound</a> &nbsp;
  <kbd>f5</kbd>&nbsp;<a href="tools/render_demo.py">demo</a> &nbsp;

</p>

**Castaway** *(working title)* is a stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the ten-hour lofi streams: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a great deal of time. She mostly idles, nodding to the music on her headphones, and every so often something happens. A message in a bottle washes straight back. A delivery drone brings a parcel, and the parcel is another pair of headphones. A shark in headphones surfaces and nods along. A coconut falls on a hermit crab, and the crab walks off wearing it. It is an unofficial remake, inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of *Johnny Castaway*, the 1992 desert-island screensaver, repainted in a sunny, hand-painted coastal anime look: 16:9, 1080p at 30 fps, and always daytime.

There are more than 90 activities, most of them on four timers that come round anywhere from every 2 to 5 minutes to once in 3 to 6 hours, and each one waits for the next bar of the music, one every 3 seconds, before it starts. So every gag lands on the beat, and in between she waits, also on the beat. Every sound is synthesized from code: no samples, no loops, no recordings.

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

The page plays a live preview and exports a YouTube-ready MP4 straight from the browser. No build step, no npm. Castaway is in development and no video has been published yet, so for now the only way to watch her wait is to run it.

<details>
<summary><b>LIST</b>: the schedule, and everything that turns up</summary>

<br>

[activities.toml](activities.toml) holds more than 90 activities (94 on 2026-10-01: 81 on four timers and 13 chained follow-ups), and other sessions add more every few hours.

| Timer | Comes round every | In a typical 10-hour run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Regular | 2 to 5 minutes | about 155 |
| Occasional | 12 to 25 minutes | about 30 |
| Rare | 30 to 60 minutes | about 13 |
| Super rare | 3 to 6 hours, at most 3 a run | about 2 |
| Chained | never on a timer: only after something else | as many as their triggers |

Typical means the median of 200 simulated runs, as the file's own header says. She is busy about a third of the time and idles the rest. Lanes let things overlap, so a ship can sail past while she is busy with a coconut, and the ship even waits for her to get busy. Every activity starts on the next bar of the music. The default run is 10:00:00 with seed 1992, which is 12000 bars, which is where the self-test number comes from.

What turns up, now and then:

- a message in a bottle, which washes straight back; a different bottle brings a reply, later
- a delivery drone, whose parcel is another pair of headphones
- a sea turtle, who visits
- a grey tabby with a white chest, who arrives on a crate, climbs the palm, naps, and one day floats away again (and comes back another time)
- the signal hunt: one bar of signal, at the very top of the palm
- a shark wearing headphones, who nods to the beat
- a tour boat full of selfie-takers
- a coconut that falls on a hermit crab, after which the coconut walks off with the crab wearing it
- a bro on an electric hydrofoil, who waves with a shaka and carves off
- "she could leave any time": she walks out over the water and comes back with an iced coffee
- bushcraft: fire by friction, a hammock, a lookout up the palm, spear fishing
- a kumara she plants, which grows over the course of the video
- and in between: coconut sipping, fishing, jogging laps, a sandcastle the tide takes, and waving for rescue, just in case

The scene keeps itself busy as well: 26 entries, 4 always-on effects and 22 timed events. Shore waves and drifting cloud shadows are built; distant birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and a rain shower are planned.

```sh
python tools/schedule.py           # validate, then simulate a 10-hour run
python tools/render_demo.py --dev  # dev reel of every activity, with a HUD
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>PLAY</b>: every sound, made from code</summary>

<br>

- Everything comes out of [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, loops or recordings, so no third-party licence applies. More than 150 sound files so far.
- The theme is a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major, a ii-V-I-vi progression over 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds, with electric piano, a kalimba lead, soft drums and vinyl crackle.
- The ocean ambience is a seamless 60-second loop too.
- The mix sits at -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP, and levels are adjustable in master and per routine.
- Nobody has listened to any of it yet. The screen above makes no sound either, which is at least period-correct for a machine with no disk in it.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>How many hours?</b> About this screen, with credits and greetz</summary>

<br>

Switch on a Japanese home computer of the early 1980s with no disk in the drive and you did not get an error. You got BASIC, straight out of ROM. The 16-bit machines first counted their memory up to a figure followed by OK, and then BASIC opened by asking how many file buffers to reserve, from 0 to 15: a question so many people met by accident that enthusiasts still keep pages explaining it. Most of them pressed Enter and hoped. A row of function-key words in reverse-video boxes sat along the bottom of the screen, and anything a program drew went on a separate graphics plane underneath the text. The 40-column machines showed a centred sign-on for about three seconds and then a flat blue screen.

This screen keeps all of that and changes what it means:

```text
 SELF-TEST ......... 12000 BARS OK. Ten hours of 3-second bars, all there
 QUESTION .......... How many hours(0-15)? Answer: 10, the default run
 FREE .............. 36000 seconds, every one of them unscheduled
 TITLE ............. the screen's own font, blown up a dot at a time and
                     made bold the cheap way: every dot drawn twice
 GRAPHICS .......... 200-line mode: every other scanline black, so solid
                     colour comes out striped; the text stays crisp on top
 KEYS .............. f1 to f10. One lights up when she does the thing
 PROMPT ............ Wait another bar (Y/N)? Answer N and it starts again
 LOOP .............. 36 seconds: twelve bars of the theme at 80 BPM
 MAKER ............. Island BASIC is made up. So is the machine

 GREETZ
 the One Bar Club ........... met at the top of the palm. Reception: 1 bar
 Kumara Watch ............... still growing. Next report at hour 10
 everyone who met the question by accident and answered it with Enter
```

- **Motion:** every change is a hard cut or a step on the beat. She nods on every beat, and so does the shark. The power cycle and the repaint take the last fifteen seconds of the loop; the first frame is the finished screen, so the name is there straight away.
- **Calm:** nothing large flashes. The cursor blinks a little faster than once a second and the waves step on the beat. With reduced motion switched on, both screens hold still on their finished frames.
- **Size:** about 77 KB and 22 KB, with no fonts and nothing external. Both bitmap fonts, the thin 8 x 16 one and the chunky 6 x 8 one, are original and live in the generator, along with the island, which is drawn in code with boxes, ellipses and lines, the way a BASIC program would draw it.
- **Not copied:** no real maker, product name, version string, copyright line, font or screen was reproduced. The question, the banner, the key labels and the picture are new, and all of them are about Castaway.

Rebuild both screens with `node src/92-japanese-basic-power-on_opus_5.5.mjs`. Castaway is unofficial and is not affiliated with the makers or owners of *Johnny Castaway*. Every club and product name on this page is made up.

</details>
